items.followUp: Construct the truth table for the AND operator.

rubric.why: Shows the input and its negated output headings.
rubric.description: Correctly labels the input and NOT output columns.

rubric.why: A NOT operator reverses each input value.
rubric.description: Gives the correct output values for inputs 0 and 1.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct truth-table values.

rubric.why: Piracy involves copying or using digital content without permission.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the copying or use is unauthorized or illegal.

rubric.why: The definition should identify the copyrighted material involved.
rubric.description: Identifies copyrighted software or other digital content.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the material as copyrighted software or digital content.

modelAnswer: Online piracy is the unauthorized copying, downloading, or distribution of copyrighted digital content over the Internet.
It may involve software, music, films, or other digital material.

rubric.why: A DoS attack aims to make a service unavailable to its users.
rubric.description: States that the attack denies or disrupts service.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that a service is made unavailable or disrupted.

rubric.why: The attack commonly overwhelms a target with excessive requests or traffic.
rubric.description: Describes how excessive requests or traffic overwhelm the target.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the overload method.

modelAnswer: A Denial of Service (DoS) attack is an attack that makes a computer or network service unavailable to its users.
It does this by flooding the target with excessive requests or traffic, overwhelming its resources.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of HTTP?

rubric.why: FTP is specifically used to transfer files.
rubric.description: States that FTP is used for file transfer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming file transfer as its purpose.

rubric.why: FTP transfers files between computers over a network.
rubric.description: Identifies the computers or network involved in the transfer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that files are transferred between computers over a network.

modelAnswer: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is used to transfer files between computers over a network.
It can be used to upload files to or download files from a server.

items.followUp: How many bits are used in an IPv4 address, and how is it written?

rubric.description: States the length of an IPv4 address.

rubric.why: IPv4 is conventionally written as four decimal numbers separated by dots.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying four numbers/octets in dotted-decimal form.

modelAnswer: IPv4 (Internet Protocol version 4) is a version of the Internet Protocol that uses 32-bit addresses.
An IPv4 address is written as four decimal numbers, called octets, separated by dots; for example, 192.168.1.1.

items.followUp: How does a web server respond to a browser request?

rubric.why: A browser obtains a web page by requesting it from a web server.
rubric.description: Explains that the browser sends a request to a web server.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the request to the server.

rubric.why: The browser receives page data and displays it to the user.
rubric.description: Explains that the browser processes received page data and displays the page.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing processing or display of the received page.

modelAnswer: A web browser sends a request for a web page to a web server using HTTP or HTTPS.
The server sends the page data back, and the browser interprets it and displays the page on the screen.

items.followUp: What is a wired network connection?

rubric.why: Wi-Fi provides network access without a physical cable, using radio waves.
rubric.description: Identifies Wi-Fi as a wireless connection using radio waves.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the wireless type or radio-wave transmission.

rubric.why: A wireless connection carries data without physical cables.
rubric.description: Defines wireless communication as data transmission without cables.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining the connection as transmission without a physical cable.

modelAnswer: A wireless connection transmits data between devices without physical cables, usually by using radio waves.

items.followUp: Write an HTML code line to create a hyperlink to a page named home.html.

rubric.why: The img tag is used to insert an image in HTML.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using the img element.

rubric.why: The src attribute specifies the image file location.
rubric.description: Includes a source attribute with an image filename or path.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including src with an image source.
